                               STATEMENT OF WORK

1.0   Introduction

      1. Montana 988 Crisis Lifeline Statewide Messaging Campaign. This work
         is being performed under the Master Media and Marketing Contract.
         a. This Statement of Work (SOW) is made and entered by and between the
             Montana Department of Public Health and Human Services (the
             Department) and TBD. This SOW incorporates by reference the terms and
             conditions of Contract Number SPB26-0600EH-XX in effect between the
             State and TBD. In case of any conflict between this SOW and the
             Contract, the Contract shall prevail. The Agency and Contractor agree as
             follows:

      2. Background
         a. On May 22, 2023, Governor Greg Gianforte signed House Bill 872 into
            law, initiating a $300 million generational investment to reform and
            enhance Montana’s behavioral health (BH) and developmental disabilities
            (DD) service systems. This core component of the governor’s Budget for
            Montana Families aims to expand intensive and community-based BH and
            DD services statewide. Starting July 2023, the Behavioral Health System
            for Future Generations (BHSFG) commission held 12 public meetings
            across Montana over 14 months, gathering extensive testimony from
            stakeholders, individuals with lived experience, and subject matter
            experts. This input shaped their final report (PDF), presented to the
            governor in September 2024. As mandated by HB 872, the report details
            recommendations for these historic investments, including 22
            recommendations and 11 Near-Term Initiatives (NTIs).
         b. This project is a result of the funding provided by recommendation number
            9 in the report.
         c. The budget for this project is $950,000 and must be fully expended by
            May 31, 2029.

      3. Objectives
         a. Increase public understanding and awareness of the 988 Lifeline and the
            behavioral health crisis support it provides.
         b. Improve access to the 988 Lifeline and its behavioral health crisis support.
         c. Develop high-utility assets that deliver immediate, measurable impact for
            the Montana 988 Crisis Lifeline Statewide Messaging Campaign that can
            be utilized by the Department for at least five years.
         d. Develop a strategy to launch and sustain the Montana 988 Crisis Lifeline
            Statewide Messaging Campaign for at least 5 years.

      4. Reference to other applicable documents
         a. To support the completion of this work, DPHHS shall provide:
              i. 988 branding guidelines and marketing materials that have been
                 developed by the state, through its partnership with the Montana State
                 University Department of Art and Architecture, referred to as “MT988”,
                 and the national 988 vendor (SAMHSA and Vibrant Emotional Health).
             ii. DPHHS Brand Guide and Writing Style Guide, and existing media
                 efforts related to 988 in Montana.
            iii. DPHHS staff person(s) on the Communications and 988 Project team
                 that will serve as the main points of contact to direct and support the
                 selected vendor in executing their work, along with monitoring
                 performance per the terms of the contract. The team will also include a
                 DPHHS financial analyst whose sole purpose is to engage with the
                 vendor on monthly budget tracking.
         b. The Contractor shall develop all required materials, reports, and strategies
             in alignment with the materials listed above, as specified by the
             Department.

3.0 Scope of Work

   1. The Contractor shall:
       a. Produce a five-year 988 marketing plan to achieve the campaign goal to be
           delivered to the Department no later than TBD. The plan must:
            i. Be developed in collaboration with the Department and informed by
               information provided by DPHHS, national, state, and local experts as
               specified by the Department.
           ii. Integrate and/or suggest ways to improve upon Montana 988 marketing
               materials, existing media partnerships (such as Montana Broadcaster’s
               Association and Northern Broadcasting System), outreach efforts
               (including MT988), and city, county, tribal, and private marketing
               initiatives.
          iii. Include key milestones, timelines, and associated costs, including those
               to the contractor and to the Department for each.
          iv. Account for the unique cultural and geographic needs of all Montanans,
               explicitly addressing barriers to access for those living in rural or frontier
               counties and historically excluded communities.
           v. Include a long-term, comprehensive approach to reduce Montana’s
               suicide rate.
          vi. Be approved by the Department prior to beginning execution of the items
               listed therein.
         vii. Note: Funding available through this Task Order will only support efforts
               toward implementation until May 31, 2029. The five-year plan is intended
               to guide future potential funding requests and strengthen partnerships
               beyond the end of this Task Order.
       b. Research strategies used by other rural peer states, such as Colorado,
           Oregon, South Dakota, and Wyoming, that launched similar programs and
           report key takeaways to the Department.
            i. The Report shall include:
                 1. A recommendation of strategies based on the strategies of other
                     rural peer states;
                 2. A description of how these strategies would be conducted in
                     Montana in the most cost-efficient and timely manner in accordance
                     with the five-year plan; and
         3. Information regarding the success of other states in reducing suicide
             rates and determining if those successes can be applied to
             Montana.
c. Recommend and implement a comprehensive marketing strategy for 988
   with a focus on the following two distinct audience segments:
    i. Direct Outreach (Priority Populations):
         1. Strategy to include the development of campaigns specifically
             designed to reach individuals in need of 988 support.
         2. Messaging must be tailored to resonate with high-risk groups,
             including youth, veterans, American Indians, and middle-aged
             Caucasian males.
   ii. Influencer Outreach (Referrers):
         1. Strategy to include the development of engagement strategies to
             equip and empower “Referrers,” which are defined as community
             partners, organizations, and/or leaders who are trusted by their
             community and have an established role in providing resources
             (and/or referrals to trusted services) to assist the population they
             serve beyond what they may be able to provide or is in the scope of
             their own services.
         2. Note: We are calling this audience “referrers” to identify them as an
             audience for the purposes of this proposal and the future contract.
             The Department is open to and looks forward to a future vendor’s
             recommendations on how to identify and name the “referrer”
             audience in external 988 messaging, if needed.
d. Recommend and implement a prioritization framework for the development
   of marketing materials that is in alignment with the Department’s objective of
   developing high-utility assets that deliver immediate, measurable impact
   across both identified audience segments listed above.
e. Develop and recommend a streamlined approach to content development
   and review that ensures the Department has ample time to review, provide
   input, and approve the proposed media strategies, materials, and budgets
   prior to production.
f. Ensure that all marketing tactics and materials are inclusive and equitable
   as determined by the Department.
g. Demonstrate how partnerships with other key stakeholders can extend the
   life of this campaign. Develop marketing materials with a minimum five-year
   shelf life for use by DPHHS and various external partners.
h. Create digital and print materials for key audiences that are plain-language
   and meet 508 accessibility standards and align with MT988 and DPHHS
    brand standards, while also considering the national 988 campaign and
    marketing efforts.
i. Develop a toolkit of these materials that key stakeholders can use if they
    secure funding outside this campaign.
j. Make recommendations and write copy for the 988 webpage that DPHHS
    manages DPHHS is currently launching a website redesign project. New
    content would be formatted into the new design.
k. Identify and work with a printing and/or fulfillment vendor to make print
    material ordering easy and accessible.
l. Provide, or facilitate through subcontract, the following services:
     i. Creative services, which could include, but are not limited to:
         1. Creative development and production;
         2. Media creation, buying, and placement; and
         3. Developing a replacement set of video PSAs (found here) that target
            our key demographic areas.
    ii. Market research and analytics, which could include, but are not limited
        to:
         1. Campaign optimization and analysis;
         2. Developing and providing regular reporting on media and marketing
            service efforts and efficacy;
         3. Evaluation of media campaign effectiveness;
         4. Confirming, tracking, analyzing, evaluating, and adjusting media
            placement; and
         5. Evaluating the effectiveness of media campaigns.
   iii. Stakeholder engagement, which could include, but is not limited to:
         1. Developing public awareness campaigns;
         2. Providing public meeting support;
         3. Conducting focus groups;
         4. Education services;
         5. Communication services;
         6. Engagement with priority populations, including, but not limited to:
            a. Rural populations;
            b. Indigenous populations;
            c. Veteran populations;
            d. Youth populations;
            e. Aging populations;
            f. Low-income populations;
            g. Pregnant populations; and
            h. Populations with disabilities.
   iv. Marketing strategic services, which could include, but are not limited to:
                1. Tactical strategy development and implementation;
                2. Ad hoc strategic input; and
                3. Developing a distribution strategy to blanket the state with the
                   MT988 posters and materials.

   2. All media, materials, and deliverables created or developed under this Task
      Order shall be reviewed and approved by the Department and/or other relevant
      reviewers identified by the Department prior to production and placement.

   3. All media, materials, and deliverables created or developed under this Task
      Order shall be the sole property of the Department. The Contractor shall not
      use, reproduce, distribute, publish, or otherwise exploit such materials for any
      purpose without the Department's prior written approval.

   4. Budget estimates must be submitted and approved by the Department for all
      proposed media and marketing projects prior to production.

   5. Marketing materials must have a minimum shelf life of 5 years, for use by
      DPHHS and various external partners

   6. Materials shall be posted in a publicly accessible file repository, such as
      Microsoft SharePoint or another location specified by the Department.

   7. Digital assets shall be accessible with alt-text and descriptions.

   8. Video assets shall include captioning that the contractor has reviewed and
      verified as accurate.


4.0 Work Approach.

   1. The project will utilize a collaborative approach that incorporates input, expertise,
      and ongoing coordination between Department officials, subject matter experts,
      and vendor representatives to ensure alignment with program goals and
      successful implementation.



5.0 Completion Criteria and Final Acceptance Criteria

   1. Completion Criteria
         a. The development of creative materials for the project will be jointly
            discussed and finalized during early planning sessions between DPHHS
            officials and the vendor. Department staff will conduct timely reviews of
            initial drafts, providing feedback and recommended revisions to ensure
            clarity, accuracy, and alignment with project goals. Ongoing coordination
            and communication will take place through Microsoft Teams meetings and
            email.
         b. Development of a five-year plan, execution of activities during the first one
            to two years, and measurable progress toward the program goals
            identified in the plan must be approved by the Department.
